主题：关于 W.A. Morgan 先生的指控。
由特别科督察劳里尔（Laurier）提出，经 C. Gimson 转呈

继本处于12月6日就 W.A. Morgan 先生一事提交的报告之后：兹报告如下，根据上述报告最后一段所述，位于静安寺路292号“Ma” Jackson 啤酒馆的服务员 Carlos Cruz 先生，未能在12月6日约定的时间和地点找到 H.J. Eddo 先生进行面谈，此后也未再见到他。次日向皇宫饭店（Palace Hotel）查询时获悉，Eddo 先生已于当日上午8时30分登上驶往香港的“拉杰普塔纳”号（S.S. "Rajputana"）轮船，他在该港口的转寄地址为香港饭店（Hongkong Hotel）。Eddo 先生并未在当地美国总领事馆登记，因为他并非上海的永久居民。仅获取了关于他的极少信息，据此认为他并非那种其言论可以不加质疑便予以采信的人。

宪兵队（Corps of Military Police）的加德纳（Gardiner）中士在接受问询时表示，他曾对 W.A. Morgan 进行过某些调查，结果显示后者是一名拳击赛事推广人，其关注军队调动仅仅是出于拳击爱好者的角度。在加德纳中士的调查过程中，他接触了一位他略知一二的水手长（Petty Officer），该水手长在回答关于 Morgan 身份的问题时回答说：“最好别说”。据信这名水手长即为怀特（White）巡官报告中提到的人。其姓名为 Somner，或发音相似的姓氏，隶属于英国皇家海军“福克斯通”号（H.M.S. "Folkestone"）。

据悉，H.J. Eddo 也将其关于 Morgan 先生涉嫌间谍活动的情报通报给了旅团司令部。

Morgan was arrested yesterday

Japanese military officials refused
to disclose the alleged crime for

vestigation but they also denied

From other Japanese sources, it

By means of a forged bill of sale,

explanation.

accomplices when they appeared at

ipal Police, he was turned over to

The police, however, received
notification of his arrest yesterday

ties were accordingly notified.

杰里·摩根（Jerry Morgan）先生，英国人，前上海拳击推广人，因涉嫌盗窃两艘日本所有的油驳船，被日本领事馆警察拘留。

日本方面扣押
杰里·摩根
涉油案

待日方审讯完毕后
将移交工部局警务处
在英国法院受审

英国臣民、前上海拳击推广人杰里·摩根先生，昨晚正被日本领事馆警察当局扣留问话，此事涉及据称企图从黄浦江浦东一侧盗窃两艘日本所有的油驳船一案。

据昨晚报道，待日本人完成对摩根的讯问后，他将被移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，以便在英国最高法院以企图盗窃罪受审。据悉，日本人正在录取他的供词，因为一名日本臣民也卷入了同一涉嫌犯罪案件，可能需要在日本领事法庭受审。

据报道，一名据称是摩根商业伙伴的中国人也被日本人抓获。据了解，他目前也正被日本民政当局拘留。

根据日本方面关于此案的报告，摩根于昨晨被捕。逮捕行动由日本海军水上警察执行，当时该名日本人和该中国人也同时被拘押。

日本军方官员拒绝透露这些人因何涉嫌犯罪而被拘留，表示需待全面调查结束后方可披露，但他们也否认这与间谍阴谋有关。

从其他日本消息来源获悉，这三人被指控企图“偷窃”两艘装满石油的驳船，这些驳船属于本市一家主要日本贸易公司。

获得许可
据称，这三名嫌疑人中的日本成员通过一张伪造的卖契，获得了移动据说停泊在浦东岸边的油驳船的许可。

随后，这些驳船被带至上海岸边，停靠在“浮水餐厅”趸船旁，此处正是日本海军水上警察总部所在地。

据进一步称，三名被告请求军警看守这些驳船，理由是“盗窃案频发”。警方同意这样做，直到驳船被移至另一锚地为止。据称，这一转移本应于昨晨进行。

与此同时，声称拥有这些驳船的日本公司的一名代表发现它们停在趸船旁，显然开始疑惑它们是如何过江的。据说他向军警要求解释。

展开调查
据日本方面对此事的报告，调查随之展开，并于昨日导致摩根及其两名同伙在出现在“浮水餐厅”趸船时被拘留。

日本方面的报告还称，由于从技术操作上日本军警无法直接将摩根移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，因此将他转交给了日本领事馆警察。

摩根在上海居住已超过12年，最广为人知的是他在过去日子里于旧卡尔登舞厅（Carlton ballroom）和市议会大厅（Town Hall）推广拳击赛事。他本人曾是拳击手，也曾做过矿工。他和他的中国合伙人在博物馆路（Museum Road）设有办事处。

虽然日本方面关于摩根被捕的说法表明逮捕发生在昨晨，但其他通常可靠的消息来源则称，这位前英国拳击推广人是在圣诞节当天被抓捕的。

然而，警方于昨日收到其被捕的通知，并据此通知了英国领事当局。

Valuable Cargo Of Oil

One Foreigner Together With Japanese And Chinese
Detained By Japanese Military Water
Police; Details Being Investigated

J. Morgan, said to be a Briton, best known in boxing and night club circles, was detained by the Japanese Military Water Police, together with two alleged accomplices, one Japanese and another Chinese, yesterday.

The three men were later handed over to civilian authorities, Morgan, it being understood, being taken into custody by the Shanghai Municipal Police.

While Japanese military authorities strenuously denied reports that the three men were implicated in an espionage plot, they refused to disclose the alleged crimes for which the men were being held, pending the conclusion of a full investigation.

It was, however, learnt from other sources that the men were being accused of having attempted to "steal" two barges loaded with oil belonging to one of the major Japanese trading companies in Shanghai.

Oil Barges Concerned

By means of a forged bill of sale, the Japanese member of the trio, it was alleged, secured a permit for the moving of the oil barges said to have been moored on the Pootung shore.

The barges were subsequently brought to the Shanghai shore and moored beside the "Floating Restaurant" pontoon, where the headquarters of the Japanese Military Water Police are located.

The military police, it was further stated, were requested to watch over the barges, as "thefts were very frequent." This the officers agreed to do until the removal of the barges to another safe anchorage, it was added. The removal was to have taken place yesterday morning, it was claimed.

The trio, however, apparently did not reckon with the sharp eye of an employee of the Japanese trading firm, which claims full ownership to the barges and their cargo.

Seeing the barges moored at the "Floating Restaurant" pontoon, this employee asked the military police for an explanation. This led to the detention for questioning of Morgan and his alleged accomplices. The names of the latter could not be learnt.

Because it was technically impossible for the Japanese military police to hand over Morgan directly to the Shanghai Municipal Police, it was understood, he was first taken to the Japanese Consular Police headquarters.

一外籍人士连同一名日本人和一名中国人
被日本海军水上警察拘留；细节正在调查中

J. 摩根，据称为英国人，在拳击和夜总会圈子里最为人熟知，昨日与两名涉嫌同伙（一名日本人，另一名中国人）一同被日本海军水上警察拘留。

这三名男子随后被移交给民政当局，据了解，摩根由上海公共租界工部局警务处收押。

虽然日本军方当局强烈否认有关这三名男子卷入间谍阴谋的报道，但他们拒绝透露这些人因何涉嫌犯罪而被拘留，表示需待全面调查结束后方可披露。

然而，从其他消息来源获悉，这些人被指控企图“偷窃”两艘装满石油的驳船，这些驳船属于上海一家主要日本贸易公司。

涉案油驳船
据称，这三名嫌疑人中的日本成员通过一张伪造的卖契，获得了移动据说停泊在浦东岸边的油驳船的许可。

随后，这些驳船被带至上海岸边，停靠在“浮水餐厅”趸船旁，此处正是日本海军水上警察总部所在地。

据进一步称，有人请求军警看守这些驳船，理由是“盗窃非常频繁”。据补充说，警官们同意这样做，直到驳船被移至另一个安全锚地为止。据称，这一转移本应于昨晨进行。

然而，这三人显然没有料到那家声称对驳船及其货物拥有完全所有权的日本贸易公司的一名员工眼光锐利。

看到驳船停靠在“浮水餐厅”趸船旁，这名员工向军警要求解释。这导致摩根及其涉嫌同伙被拘留问话。后者的姓名未能获知。

据了解，由于从技术操作上日本军警无法直接将摩根移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，他首先被带往日本领事馆警察总部。

Mr. Jerry Morgan, long-time

new regulations recently pro-

mitting offenses against the

subject to martial law.

MORGAN:

William Alfred "Jerry" Morgan, British
subject, was born in Calcutta, India, on 27th
September, 1890. He is in possession of
British passport No.C25700 issued in Shanghai
on 9th July, 1937, and is registered with the
local British Consular Authorities.

Morgan is reported to have spent most of
his youth in Australia and New Zealand and to
have subsequently served with the Royal Engineers,
receiving his discharge in Hongkong. He has been
a resident of Shanghai for many years but though
describing himself as a "Mining and Mineral Ores,"
Consulting Engineer, has never practised his
profession in this city and has never been in
regular employment.

Morgan is best known in Shanghai as a
gambler and a promoter of sporting events; he
has variously been manager of the Pacific Club,
a gambling establishment which was closed by the
Police in 1933, Secretary of the International
Country Club, manager of the Lafayette Gardens
and manager of the Albert Gardens. For some
time he was well known in local boxing circles
and refereed fights at the Auditorium, but was
eventually barred because of his corrupt
practices. He has been a continual source of

Jerry Morgan
Is Released By
Court On Bail

Briton Asks Freedom,
Alleges Harsh Treat-
ment By Japanese

Arraigned for the second time
before the British Police Court yes-
terday afternoon, William Alfred
Morgan, popularly known as Jerry
Morgan, heard that he was being
charged for attempting to receive a
quantity of wood oil on December
25 knowing the same to be stolen.

Mr. E. L. Hartopp, appearing for
the Crown Advocate, requested that
the case be adjourned for one week
to allow the crown to investigate
the case thoroughly. Mr. C. H.
Haines, magistrate, granted this ad-
journment, stating that the case
will be heard on Friday, January 7,
at 10 a.m. He also explained to
Morgan that the adjournment was
granted to enable the crown to in-
vestigate the charge, and should it
be justified and sustained, his case
would then be arraigned before H.
M. Supreme Court.

Morgan replied that in view of the
unnecessarily harsh treatment he
received during the period he was
detained by the Japanese, he
begged to request the court to re-
lease him on bail. In answer to
this Magistrate Haines pointed out
that he could not take into con-
sideration the accused's suffering,
but that he was free to go on his
own recognizance and on two es-
surances of $250 each that he would
appear in court on the morning of
January 7. These were produced
yesterday evening.

Arrested Xmas Day

Mr. Morgan, was arrested in the
afternoon of December 25 for al-
legedly attempting to receive two
barges of wood oil belonging to a
Japanese concern, knowing this
quantity of oil to be stolen. He
was arrested on the Peking Road
Bund, beside the Floating Re-
staurant.

Morgan was handed over to the
Shanghai Municipal Police on
Wednesday evening. He was turn-
ed over to the custody of Detec-
tive Sub-Inspector J. G. Crighton
at 6.50 p.m. in the presence of Mr.
S. Okamoto, Japanese Consul-
General, and Mr. A. G. N. Ogden,
British Consul.

Formerly a soldier, a miner, boxer,
and more recently a boxing pro-
moter, Jerry Morgan was first
brought before Mr. Haines at the
British Police Court yesterday
morning. No persons appearing to
make a complaint against Morgan,
Mr. Haines adjourned the hearing
until 3 o'clock yesterday afternoon,
stating that if by this time the
Japanese authorities failed to re-
gister a complaint he would be com-
pelled to set Morgan at liberty.

Enter Bruce Lockhart

The Japanese complaint was re-
gistered, but the brief preliminary
hearing was disturbed yesterday
afternoon by the sudden appearance
of Mr. Bruce Lockhart. Mr. Lock-
hart strode into the courtroom
while the hearing was being con-
ducted and, walking up to Morgan,
slipped him a document. Magis-
trate Haines immediately demand-
ed to know the cause of this inter-
ruption. The document was not
given to Morgan, but was kept by
D.S.-I. Crighton. Later it was re-
vealed that it was Morgan's state-
ment to the court—compiled, Mr.
Morgan told THE CHINA PRESS later,
by Lockhart on information received
from Morgan.

In this statement, which is un-
signed, apparently because Morgan
had no opportunity to see it yet,
the former soldier-miner-boxer is
on record as claiming that he was
deliberately kidnapped by a trick and
detained for five days and four
nights under the "most harsh and
cruel conditions" within a few hund-
red yards of H.B.M.'s Consulate-
General at Shanghai.

Morgan Gives Version

Morgan's version of the affair is
stated in the document as follows
(in part):

"On the morning of December 25,
about 11 a.m., I was taking a bath
at my residence in Weihaiwei Road.
I was informed that a Chinese
wished to see me, and met this in-
dividual, who said that some ques-
tion had arisen concerning a busi-
ness transaction in connection with
tung oil in barges of which I had
a partial cognizance. He had a
hire car waiting outside, and asked
me to go down to the Bund jetty
at once.

"I did so, but immediately I
boarded one of the barges tied up
next to the Floating Restaurant,
the Chinese vanished. After a few
minutes a Japanese in civilian
clothes approached me, asked for
my card, gave me his, and request-
ed in English that I step off the
barge and go to the Floating Re-
staurant, which I did.

"I was ushered into a compart-
ment where a Japanese in military
uniform was sitting. He spoke poor
English, but understood my explana-
tions that I was an Englishman. I
turned to leave, but found my pass-
age barred, and that I was held a
prisoner. Permission to use the
telephone was denied me, and I was
held incommunicado.

Protests Disregarded

"Later that same afternoon a
Japanese who spoke English ques-
tioned me. I protested strongly
against the detention and demand-
ed that the British Consular au-
thorities be instantly informed of
my plight. No notice was taken of
my demand.

"I was held prisoner on the Re-
staurant for the night of December
25, the day and night of December
26, and the days and nights of
December 27 and 28. On Wednes-
day, December 29, Mr. Ogden,
British Consul, appeared at about
5 p.m., and I was released into the
custody of the Shanghai Municipal
Police, spending the night of
December 29 in a cell at the Cen-
tral Police Station.

"I wish to state that the treat-
ment I received at the hands of
Japanese military and consular
officials on that pontoon during the
five days and four nights I was held
prisoner was unnecessarily harsh,
inhumane and uncivilized. I was
not allowed to sleep during this
long period. There was a chair, but
no bed nor pallet on which I
might rest. I was not allowed to
lie down on the floor by my guards,
who were a Japanese soldier and
two Chinese policemen imported
from North China. There were
neither washing nor lavatory
facilities, and the meager food pro-
vided was rice and cabbage with
Chinese tea.

"As I was moved from one com-
partment to the other at intervals,
it was bitterly cold, for one of the
compartments was completely ex-
posed to the weather and the other
had windows, the glass of which was
broken. I was given no covering of
any kind at nights, and had to
spend the nights shivering on my
chair."

Interviewed by a representative
of THE CHINA PRESS Jerry Morgan
stated that he was connected with
this transaction via his compadre,
C. A. Chow. He was sure that the
compadre had no knowledge that
the property was stolen, for he
trusted him implicitly, but that he
led him into it unwittingly.

"I feel sure that I am on safe
ground," he concluded.

杰里·摩根
获法庭保释

英国人要求自由，
指控日本人待
遇残酷

威廉·阿尔弗雷德·摩根（William Alfred Morgan），人称杰里·摩根（Jerry Morgan），昨日下午第二次在英国警察法庭受审，获悉他被控于12月25日企图收受一批桐油，且明知该批桐油系赃物。

代表王室检察官出庭的 E. L. 哈托普（E. L. Hartopp）先生请求将案件延期一周，以便王室方面对案件进行彻底调查。治安法官 C. H. 海恩斯（C. H. Haines）先生批准了这一延期申请，并宣布案件将于1月7日（星期五）上午10时审理。他还向摩根解释，批准延期是为了让王室方面调查该项指控，如果指控成立并有据可依，他的案件随后将被移送至英王陛下最高法院受审。

摩根回答说，鉴于他在被日本人拘留期间受到了不必要的残酷对待，他恳请法庭准予保释。针对这一请求，海恩斯治安法官指出，他不能考虑被告所受的苦难，但摩根可以具结悔过，并由两名各提供250美元保证金的保证人担保，确保其于1月7日上午出庭。这两名保证人已于昨晚找到。

圣诞节当日被捕

摩根先生于12月25日下午被捕，涉嫌企图收受属于一家日本商行的两驳船桐油，且明知这批油系被盗。他是在外滩北京路码头，紧邻“浮动餐厅”（Floating Restaurant）的地方被捕的。

周三晚间，摩根被移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处。当晚6时50分，在日本总领事 S. Okamoto 先生和英国领事 A. G. N. Ogden 先生在场的情况下，他被移交给侦探副督察 J. G. Crighton 监管。

杰里·摩根曾是一名士兵、矿工、拳击手，近期更成为拳击推广人，他于昨日上午首次在海恩斯先生主持的英国警察法庭出庭。由于无人出面控告摩根，海恩斯先生将听证会推迟至昨日下午3时，并表示如果届时日本当局仍未提出控告，他将不得不释放摩根。

布鲁斯·洛克哈特介入

日本方面提出了控告，但昨日下午简短的预审因布鲁斯·洛克哈特（Bruce Lockhart）先生的突然出现而受到干扰。洛克哈特先生在听证进行期间大步走进法庭，走到摩根面前，塞给他一份文件。海恩斯治安法官立即要求说明此次打断的原因。该文件并未交给摩根，而是由侦探副督察 Crighton 扣留。后来透露，那是摩根向法庭提交的陈述书——摩根后来告诉《字林西报》（THE CHINA PRESS），该陈述书由洛克哈特根据从摩根处获得的信息编写而成。

在这份未签名的陈述书中（显然因为摩根尚无机会有机会审阅），这位前士兵-矿工-拳击手声称，他是被诡计故意绑架，并在距离英国驻上海总领事馆仅几百码的地方，在“最严酷和残忍的条件”下被拘禁了五天四夜。

摩根陈述事件经过

文件中陈述的摩根版本如下（部分）：

“12月25日上午约11时，我正在威海卫路的住所洗澡。有人告知我有一位中国人想见我，我见到了这个人，他说关于我所略知一二的一批驳船桐油的商业交易出现了一些问题。外面停着一辆出租车，他让我立刻去外滩码头。

“我照做了，但我一登上停靠在‘浮动餐厅’旁边的一艘驳船，那个中国人就消失了。几分钟后，一名身穿便服的日本人走近我，索要我的名片，给了我他的名片，并用英语要求我走下驳船前往‘浮动餐厅’，我照办了。

“我被引到一个隔间，里面坐着一名身穿军装的日本人。他英语讲得不好，但听懂了我解释我是英国人。我转身欲离开，却发现去路被阻，我成了囚犯。我被拒绝使用电话，并与外界隔绝。

抗议被无视

“当天下午晚些时候，一名会说英语的日本人审问了我。我对拘留提出强烈抗议，并要求立即通知英国领事当局我的困境。我的要求未被理会。

“我在‘浮动餐厅’被囚禁过夜，度过了12月25日夜晚、12月26日全天及夜晚，以及12月27日和28日的全天及夜晚。12月29日（星期三）下午5时许，英国领事 Ogden 先生出现，我被移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处监管，12月29日晚在中央捕房的一间牢房里度过。

“我要声明，在我被囚禁的五天四夜里，日本军方和领事官员在那艘趸船上对我的待遇是不必要的严酷、不人道且不文明。在这段漫长的时间里，我不被允许睡觉。那里有一把椅子，但没有床或垫子供我休息。看守我的卫兵——一名日本士兵和两名从华北调来的中国警察——不允许我躺在地板上。那里没有洗漱或如厕设施，提供的少量食物是米饭、白菜和中国茶。

“由于我被间歇性地从一个隔间转移到另一个隔间，天气极其寒冷，因为其中一个隔间完全暴露在风雨中，而另一个隔间的窗户玻璃破碎。夜间我没有得到任何覆盖物，只能坐在椅子上瑟瑟发抖地度过夜晚。”

《字林西报》记者采访杰里·摩根时，他表示自己是通过他的伙伴 C. A. Chow 卷入这起交易的。他确信他的伙伴不知道财产是被盗的，因为他完全信任他，但对方在不知情的情况下将他引入了此事。

“我确信我是站在安全立场上的，”他总结道。

Briton Held by
Japanese Naval
Guard at Jetty

Mr. W. A. Morgan Detained
for Alleged Theft

HANDED OVER TO BRITISH
CONSULATE-GENERAL

A British subject, Mr. W. A.
Morgan, was being held yesterday
under a naval guard at the former
Floating Restaurant, Peking Road
Jetty, following his arrest on the
afternoon of Christmas Day by
Japanese military police. He is ac-
cused by them of the attempted theft
of a cargo of wood oil from Pootung,
and had been kept in custody in the
Floating Restaurant since Boxing
Day, the "North-China Daily News"
was informed yesterday. Following
representations by the British Con-
sular authorities, and a visit to the
Floating Restaurant by a party of
S.M.P. detectives, including a Japan-
ese officer, Mr. Morgan was handed
over to the S. M. Police at 7 p.m.
yesterday, and will appear in H.M.
Police Court this morning.

A Japanese report last night stated
that Mr. Morgan was detained by
the Japanese Military Water Police,
together with two alleged accom-
plices, one Japanese and a Chinese,
yesterday. The three men were later
handed over to the civil authorities,
Morgan being taken into custody by
the S.M. Police. While the Japanese
military authorities, the report stated,
strongly denied reports that the
three men were implicated in an
espionage scheme, they refused to
disclose the alleged crimes for which
they were being held, pending the
conclusion of a full investigation.

Other Japanese sources, however,
stated that the men were being ac-
cused of having attempted to steal
two barges loaded with oil belonging
to one of the major Japanese trading
companies in Shanghai. The Japan-
ese member of the trio is said to
have secured a permit for the removal
of the oil barges said to have been
on the Pootung shore.

Barges Guarded

The barges were eventually brought
across to Shanghai, and moored
beside the Floating Restaurant Pon-
toon, where the headquarters of the
Japanese Military Water Police are
located. The military police, it was
further stated, were requested to
watch over the barges, as "thefts
were very frequent." This the
officers agreed to do until the removal
of the barges to another safe an-
chorage, it was added, and the re-
moval was to have taken place yes-
terday morning.

An employee of the Japanese trad-
ing firm, which claims full ownership
over thee barges and their cargo, says
the Japanese report, saw the barges
moored at the Floating Restaurant
and asked the military police for an
explanation. This is said to have
led to the detention for questioning
of Morgan and his alleged accom-
plices. Because it was technically
impossible for the Japanese Military
Police to hand over Morgan to the
Shanghai Municipal Police, he was
first taken to the Japanese Consular
Police headquarters, the Japanese
report concluded.

英国人在码头
被日本海军
卫兵扣押

W. A. 摩根先生因涉嫌
盗窃被拘留

移交英国总领事馆

据昨日获悉，英国臣民 W. A. 摩根先生于圣诞节下午被日本宪兵逮捕后，昨日一直在北京路码头原“浮动餐厅”处由海军卫兵看守。日本方面指控他企图盗窃来自浦东的一船桐油，并且自节礼日（Boxing Day）以来一直被关押在“浮动餐厅”内。据《字林西报》昨日获悉，在英国领事当局交涉以及包括一名日本军官在内的上海公共租界工部局警务处侦探小组访问“浮动餐厅”后，摩根先生于昨晚7时被移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，并将于今晨在英王陛下警察法庭出庭。

日本方面昨晚的一份报告称，摩根先生昨日被日本军事水上警察拘留，另有两名涉嫌同伙，一名日本人和一名中国人。这三名男子随后被移交给民事当局，摩根由上海公共租界工部局警务处收押。该报告称，虽然日本军方当局强烈否认这三名男子卷入间谍计划的报道，但他们拒绝透露他们被拘留所涉的所谓罪行，以待全面调查结束。

然而，其他日本消息来源称，这些人被指控企图偷窃两艘装满油的驳船，这些驳船属于上海一家主要日本贸易公司。据说这三名团伙中的日本成员获得了移除据称停在浦东岸边的油驳船的许可证。

驳船受监护

据进一步称，驳船最终被拖至上海，停泊在“浮动餐厅”趸船旁，那里是日本军事水上警察总部所在地。此外还称，军方警察被要求看守驳船，因为“盗窃案非常频繁”。据补充说，军官们同意这样做，直到驳船被转移到另一个安全的锚地，而转移工作原定于昨天上午进行。

据日本方面的报告称，一家声称拥有这些驳船及其货物全部所有权的日本贸易公司的雇员看到驳船停泊在“浮动餐厅”，并向军方警察询问解释。据说这导致了对摩根及其涉嫌同伙的拘留审讯。日本方面的报告最后得出结论，由于日本军事警察在技术上无法将摩根移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，他首先被带往日本领事警察总部。
